correctness.rationale: For each prime p, let a_n=v_p(f_n). Hypotheses f_1|f_2 and f_n|f_{n+2} give a_1<=a_2 and monotonicity separately along parity classes. Verified the shifted-interval lemma by pairing equal-parity positions, with the exceptional even-start odd-length final even term compared to a_1 using a_{s+2h}>=a_2>=a_1. It gives each ordinary generalized binomial valuation >=0. For width j the column valuation b_n=sum_{i=n}^{n+j-1}a_i-sum_{i=1}^j a_i has b_1=0, b_2=a_{j+1}-a_1>=0 and b_{n+2}>=b_n; the same lemma proves every generalized binomial coefficient in every column integral for every N,K,j,p. This handles all unbounded quantifiers, not just initial terms. Verified semigroup examples H_q=<2,2q+1> are ComboSum by closure under addition, not ordinary chains because f_2=p and f_3=1; the factor at 2r for odd prime r>=2q+1 gives 1/p and rules out Shapiro divisor-product form. Checked periodic valuations (0,1,1) yield a three-step analogue failing in column two with B_{C2}(4,2)=1/2. Independently generated 500 random parity-monotone finite valuation sequences and checked every available column, confirming the finite consequences but not replacing the interval proof.

originality.rationale: Shapiro (2023) proves divisor chains and divisor-product sequences binomid at every level, and explicitly asks whether all ComboSum sequences are. The current two-step parity-divisibility sufficient condition is a distinct implication, because its natural semigroup examples fail both stated sufficient conditions. It supplies a rigorously identified proper ComboSum subclass, not a resolution of the unrestricted question. The Caalim–Tanaka finite-index extension problem addresses a different object. Priority uncertainty remains for stronger interval-majorization sufficient criteria not found by exact/general searches.
residual_risks: An implicit two-parity interval-majorization theorem in earlier number-theory literature could subsume the proof.
Caalim–Tanaka full text was not inspected; only the described finite-index scope was compared.
No claim that all ComboSum sequences are binomid at every level.

value.rationale: The binomid-pyramid all-level integrality problem is explicitly motivated by an open sufficient-condition/ComboSum question. A concise but genuinely nontrivial valuation lemma handles infinitely many column widths, and the semigroup family demonstrates coverage beyond familiar sufficient hypotheses. The three-step counterexample isolates a meaningful structural boundary rather than an arbitrary finite case. No claim of complete characterization or solution to the full ComboSum question.
